children: China's strong trade momentum likely persisted in August, according to BofA Securities in a research note. The country's export growth in dollar terms is expected to reaccelerate to 25% on year in August from 23.9% in July, supported by continued strength in chip and automobile shipments, the bank says. Import growth likely eased modestly to 26% on year from 27.5%, it adds. Strong technology imports were partly offset by a renewed decline in crude arrivals indicated by high-frequency tanker data, they add. (tracy.qu@wsj.com)
